ma_hokum_rock.blurb: A single large glacial erratic on Cape Cod, standing beside Scargo Lake in the town of Dennis. It is a small-scale outing: the block is only about twelve feet tall, so the eleven problems are short and the whole visit takes an hour or two. Grades run from a near-beginner line up to one very hard problem, with most of the rest in the V2 to V3 range and a single V5. The boulder sits in shade, which helps on warm days. One line carries a run-out warning, so bring a pad and a spotter. Worth a stop if you are on the Cape and have no other rock nearby.

ma_titanic_boulder.blurb: A standout single block in the Wallum Lake boulderfields of Douglas State Forest, in central Massachusetts. Eleven problems cover a wide spread, from an easy V1 up to V7, with a cluster of V4 and V5 lines in the middle. The big prize is a prow problem that begins under a roof and moves into compression; a slab at V6 suits those who prefer friction. The walk from the main lot is about ten minutes on a rocky, twisting trail, and the boulder stands right next to the path. Bring pads for the roof line.
ma_titanic_boulder.approach: From the northwest corner of the lot, follow the main trail west for a few minutes, turn left onto the Basin Marsh Trail, pass two other boulders, and keep going on the rocky trail; the boulder is beside the path, about ten minutes in total.

ma_extraterrestrial_rock.blurb: One of the first blocks you meet on the main trail at Rocky Pond in Boylston, a short drive from Worcester. The gritty granite offers eleven problems with a good range: several in the V0 to V3 band, a pair at V7 and V8, and a few easy lines that make it friendly to newcomers. Two crack features set it apart from most Massachusetts bouldering, a diagonal crack on the back face and a layback crack on the south side. A low-angle slab on the trail side is the gentlest option. Heights are modest, so crash pads are the standard protection.

ma_cavalry_boulder.blurb: A big boulder near the crest of a hill in the central part of the Cavalry boulder field on Cape Ann, north of Boston. The block is tall enough that many lines feel like highballs, and the eleven problems range from an easy V0 through a block of V3 and V5 lines to a V10 testpiece, plus one top-rope line. The field is secluded and shaded by hemlocks, so it stays cooler than open crags. Take friends and plenty of pads, since the heights ask for spotters. It is easy to recognise once you reach the top of the rise.

ma_hard_knocks_boulder.blurb: A small, roughly ten-foot boulder at the southern end of College Rock in Hopkinton, sitting on the west side of the dirt road past the main cliff. Ten problems are packed into it, mostly easy to moderate: a handful at VB to V1, a few in the V2 to V4 range, and one hard line at V7. It makes a handy warm-up or side trip after a day on the crag's top-ropes. The woods are damp, and the rock can feel slick on humid days, so pick a dry, cool day. Short climbs mean a couple of pads and a spotter are plenty.

ma_townsend_conjecture_overhang.blurb: A compact, steep, exposed face of sharp rock in West Townsend, the first good boulder you reach among the State Line Boulders. Ten problems start low under the overhang: several easy lines at the bottom end, a middle band of V2 to V4, then V6 and V7 classics on the central section. The rock is abrasive, so tape helps. Leaves and needles gather on the top-outs and loose rock sits on the right-hand walk-off, so check before topping out. Bring at least two pads, since the landing slopes. The site is wooded and approached by bushwhack.

ma_queen_s_row_boulders.blurb: A small boulder garden within the Stone Tower section of Lynn Woods, north of Boston, and a short walk from the Great Woods Road lot. Ten problems fill it, starting at an easy V0 and rising through a solid V1 to V4 middle to two V7 lines at the top end. The best-regarded problems are a face and an arete in the V2 to V4 range. It is a pleasant place to scramble between boulders and suits a short session. The granite is coarse, and heights are low, so a couple of pads usually suffice.
ma_queen_s_row_boulders.approach: Walk up Great Woods Road for about five minutes, take the first left at the trail junction, go a short way, then turn right; the boulders are on your right after about another minute.

ma_n_wall_includes_o_wall.blurb: A short stretch of the old granite quarry cliffs in Quincy, southeast of Boston, where the N Wall and its neighbour the O Wall run together. Climbing here is mostly low bouldering, with two easy top-rope lines on the cliff. Problems are mainly V0 to V2 with a pair near V6, plus a short arete on the O Wall with a view toward the city skyline. The alcove tends to stay wet, so go after dry weather. Walls are short, so pads and a spotter cover most of it.
